questions.stem: Methane and oxygen can exist together at room temperature without reacting, even though combustion is highly exothermic. Why?

options.text: Because methane and oxygen do not collide at room temperature
Because the particles do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy barrier
Because a catalyst is needed for all combustion reactions
Because the reaction is actually endothermic at room temperature

questions.explanation: Even though combustion of methane is exothermic, the particles at room temperature do not have enough kinetic energy to overcome the activation energy barrier. A spark or flame is needed to provide the initial activation energy to start the reaction.

questions.stem: On a reaction profile diagram, where is the activation energy measured from?

options.text: From the products to the peak (transition state)
From the reactants to the products
From the reactants to the peak (transition state)
From the baseline to the reactants

questions.explanation: Activation energy is the energy difference between the reactants and the peak of the reaction profile (the transition state). It represents the energy barrier that must be overcome for the reaction to proceed.
